corpus.title: Reference corpus
corpus.intro: Reference documents the platform may cite when explaining a result. They never change the level or the routing: they only enrich the explanation.
corpus.noDeleteNote: A document is added and retired, never deleted. Retiring keeps the record, which is the only thing that keeps older reports explainable.
corpus.citationHint: How this document will be cited in a report.
corpus.localeHint: Retrieval respects language: a document is only used in its own.
corpus.textHint: Split into chunks when saved. Under “citation only” there is a length cap, and text above it is refused whole rather than trimmed.
corpus.scopesIntro: Where this document may be used: a module, a safety rule, a clinical source or, exceptionally, everything.
corpus.generalScopeNote: “General” should be rare: a document with no scope is retrieved for everything.
corpus.rightsIntro: Without a rights declaration and its evidence, a document is neither published nor indexed. The service decides that, not this screen.
corpus.changelogHint: Kept in the corpus history. At least 3 characters.
corpus.evidenceHint: Stored as evidence for the declaration.

scopeKeyHint.general: No key: it applies to everything.

rightsMeaning.own_document: Written by The Somnus. No further evidence needed.
rightsMeaning.open_access: Published under an open licence. Give the licence and the link.
rightsMeaning.licensed: Covered by an institutional subscription or purchase. Give the licence and who holds it.
rightsMeaning.citation_only: The citation and a short summary only. The platform holds no full text.

rightsWarning.licensed: Careful: declaring “licensed” asserts that a real subscription or purchase covers this use. If none does, the text ends up sent to an external provider with no right to it.
rightsWarning.citation_only: Careful: “citation only” asserts there is no full text here. There is a length cap, and longer text is refused whole rather than trimmed: if you need the full article, declare the rights that permit it.

setup.heading: Create your encrypted Drive
setup.intro: Everything you keep here is encrypted in your browser before it leaves it. Neither The Somnus nor Google can read it: only you and the people you share each folder with.
setup.point1: Choose a passphrase just for the Drive. It is not your sign-in link and it is never sent to the server.
setup.point2: You will get a recovery code. It is the only way back in if you forget the passphrase.
setup.point3: If you lose both the passphrase and the code, nobody can recover your files. Not even us.
setup.passphraseHint: At least 12 characters. A long phrase beats a strange word: "black-coffee-on-the-night-shift".
setup.tooShort: The passphrase needs at least 12 characters.
setup.mismatch: The two passphrases do not match.

guideContent.heading: How to use the Encrypted Drive
guideContent.s1Body: The first time, you choose a passphrase just for the Drive and get a recovery code. The passphrase never leaves your browser. Keep the code off the computer. If you lose both, nobody can recover your files.
guideContent.s2Body: Every shared folder has its own key. Create one per topic: "Safety protocols", "Algorithm rules", "Shift instructions". Inside you can create subfolders and notes, and upload files of up to 20 MB.
guideContent.s3Body: "New note" lets you write right in the console: the steps of a protocol, how a rule is applied, instructions for the team. Every save creates a new version, encrypted and signed by you.
guideContent.s4Body: In "People" you choose a colleague and a permission. "Read only" can view and download; "Can edit" can also create, upload, rename and move; "Owner" can also share and delete forever. Only colleagues who set up their Drive appear.
guideContent.s5Body: Each person has a ten-group fingerprint. Compare it once by phone or in person and press "I checked the fingerprint". If someone's key changes you will see a red warning: confirm with them before accepting the new key.
guideContent.s6Body: When you remove someone, the folder key changes for everyone who stays. Anything uploaded afterwards cannot be opened with their old copy.
guideContent.s7Body: Whatever you move to the trash can be restored. Only an owner deletes it forever. The Drive locks itself after 15 minutes of inactivity and when you sign out; your passphrase opens it again.
guideContent.s8Body: This Drive is for internal team material. Do not upload patient data, reports about specific people or anything that identifies someone. The platform's clinical flows exist for that.
